name.text: Volumes of Solids of Revolution-Washer method-q1

questiontext.text:
Find the volume of the solid generated by revolving the region bounded by \(y = {@f1(x)@}\) and \(y = {@f2(x)@}\) about the \(x\)‐axis.

Here is a sketch of the bounded region with the axis of rotation shown,

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [{#minx#}, {#maxy#}, {#maxx#}, {#miny#}], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation: false }); // Define the functions var f1 = function(x) { return x*x + {#const1#}; }; var f2 = function(x) { return x + {#const2#}; }; // Plot the curves var curve1 = board.create('functiongraph', [f1, -3, 3], { strokeColor: 'blue' }); var curve2 = board.create('functiongraph', [f2, -3, 3], { strokeColor: 'red' }); // Find the intersection points var interPoint1 = board.create('intersection', [curve1, curve2, 0], { visible: true, name:'\\(({#a#},{#x1#})\\)'}); var interPoint2 = board.create('intersection', [curve1, curve2, 1], { visible: true, name:'\\(({#b#},{#y1#})\\)'}); // Find the minimum point of the curve var minPoint = board.create('point', [0, f1(0)], { style: 5, size: 4, fillColor: 'green', strokeColor: 'green', visible: false}); var minPointY = minPoint.Y(); // Create the first curly bracket var height1 = 0.5; // height of the first curly bracket var crl1 = board.create('curve', [[0],[0]], {strokeWidth:1, strokeColor:'black' }, {visible: false}); crl1.bezierDegree = 3; crl1.updateDataArray = function() { var A = minPoint, B = board.create('point', [minPoint.X(), 0], {visible: false}); var d = [B.X() - A.X(), B.Y() - A.Y()]; var dl = Math.sqrt(d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1]); var mid = [(A.X() + B.X()) * 0.5, (A.Y() + B.Y()) * 0.5]; d[0] *= height1 / dl; d[1] *= height1 / dl; this.dataX = [ A.X(), A.X() - d[1], mid[0], mid[0] - d[1], mid[0], B.X() - d[1], B.X() ]; this.dataY = [ A.Y(), A.Y() + d[0], mid[1], mid[1] + d[0], mid[1], B.Y() + d[0], B.Y() ]; }; // Text for the first curly bracket var txt1 = board.create('text', [ function() { var A = minPoint, B = board.create('point', [minPoint.X(), 0], {visible: false}); var B = board.create('point', [2, 0], {visible: false}); var d = [B.X() - A.X(), B.Y() - A.Y()]; var dl = Math.sqrt(d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1]); var mid = [(A.X() + B.X()) * 0.5, (A.Y() + B.Y()) * 0.5]; d[0] *= height2 / dl; d[1] *= height2 / dl; this.dataX = [ A.X(), A.X() - d[1], mid[0], mid[0] - d[1], mid[0], B.X() - d[1], B.X() ]; this.dataY = [ A.Y(), A.Y() + d[0], mid[1], mid[1] + d[0], mid[1], B.Y() + d[0], B.Y() ]; var d = [B.X() - A.X(), B.Y() - A.Y()]; var dl = Math.sqrt(d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1]); var mid = (A.X() + B.X()) * 0.5; d[1] *= height2 / dl; return mid - d[1] + 0.1; }, function() { var A = board.create('point', [2, f1(2)], {visible: false}); generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We will use the Washer method formula to find the volume of the solid generated by revolving the region bounded \(y = {@f1(x)@}\) and \(y = {@f2(x)@}\) about the \(x\)‐axis,

Let's first find the points of intersection:

\({@f1(x)@} = {@f2(x)@}\)

\({@f1(x)-f2(x)@} = 0\)

\({@factor(f1(x)-f2(x))@} = 0\)

\(x = {@b@}\) or \(x = {@a@}\)

The limits of integration will be from \( {@a@}\) to \({@b@}\) (the \(x\)-values where the curves intersect).

The formula for this case would be:

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \int_{a}^{b} \big((f(x))^2 - (g(x))^2\big) \, dx\)

Where \(f(x)\) is the outer function and \(g(x)\) is the inner function.

Given \(f(x)= {@f2(x)@}\) and \(g(x)= {@f1(x)@}\) about the \(x\)‐axis, we'll find the volume using the washer method formula:

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \int_{{@a@}}^{{@b@}} \big (\big( {@f2(x)@} \big)^2 - \big( {@f1(x)@} \big)^2 \big) \, dx\)

Let's solve this integral:

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \int_{{@a@}}^{{@b@}} \big (\big( {@f2(x)@} \big)^2 - \big( {@f1(x)@} \big)^2 \big) \, dx\)

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \int_{{@a@}}^{{@b@}} \big (\big( {@eqn1@} \big) - \big( {@eqn2@} \big) \big) \, dx\)

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \int_{{@a@}}^{{@b@}} \big ( {@eqn3@} \big) \, dx\)

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \left ( {@eqn4@} \right)_{{@a@}}^{{@b@}} \)

\( \displaystyle V = \pi \left(\big({@eqn5@}\big) - \big({@eqn6@}\big)\right) \)

\(\displaystyle V = \pi \left({@eqn7@}\right)\)

\(V = \boxed{{@volume@} \approx {@decimalplaces(volume,2)@} }\)
